facts.text: On this date in 1492, Columbus made landfall in the Bahamas — but he died convinced he had reached Asia, never acknowledging he had found continents unknown to Europeans.
On October 12, 1810, Munich held its first Oktoberfest to celebrate a royal wedding. The festival was so popular it became annual, shifted earlier to catch better weather.
Manila is the world's most densely populated city proper, cramming over 70,000 people per square kilometer — denser than any comparably sized area on Earth.
More people live inside a circle drawn 4,000 km around Bangkok than outside it — over half the world's population fits in that single Asian hemisphere.
Canada has more lakes than every other country on Earth combined, holding roughly 60% of the world's fresh surface lake water within its borders.
On this date in 1987, markets were five trading days from Black Monday. The Dow had already fallen 15% in the preceding weeks — the crash wasn't a surprise to charts, only to confidence.
On October 12, 1492, Columbus landed in the Bahamas. Spain's crown had funded the voyage for roughly 2 million maravedis — less than the annual salary of a senior Castilian bureaucrat.
The New York Stock Exchange was founded under a buttonwood tree in 1792 by 24 brokers. The agreement they signed was 43 words long.
Saudi Aramco briefly hit a $2.4 trillion valuation in 2022 — making it worth more than the entire GDP of Italy, a G7 nation.
The U.S. penny costs 3.69 cents to produce. The government loses money on every one it mints, and has for over two decades.
On this date in 1967, the Outer Space Treaty entered into force — meaning no nation can legally claim the Moon, and nuclear weapons are formally banned from orbit.
On October 12, 1999, Earth's population officially crossed 6 billion. It has since added nearly 2 billion more people in under three decades.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
Your body contains about 37 trillion cells, yet bacterial and other microbial cells in and on you roughly match that number — you are, by count, nearly half not-you.
Light from the Sun takes 8 minutes to reach Earth, but the photons themselves were generated in the Sun's core up to 100,000 years ago, trapped by the density of plasma before finally escaping.
On this day in 1492, Columbus landed in the Bahamas — the same year the Aztec Empire was at its absolute peak, a civilization he never knew existed and never reached.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded. Europe's oldest university predates an entire New World civilization.
On this day in 1810, the first Oktoberfest was held in Munich — as a royal wedding celebration. It was not supposed to become an annual event.
The fax machine was patented in 1843, a full 23 years before the typewriter. You could transmit a document before you could mechanically type one.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. The ancient world was ancient even to the ancients.
Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, 2012 — and already feels ancient.
Hiraeth (Welsh, n.): a longing for a home you cannot return to, or that never existed. Untranslatable, it carries grief, nostalgia, and belonging braided into a single breath.
On this day in 1492, Columbus made landfall. The Taíno word he recorded most — 'canoa' — became canoe, one of the first American words absorbed into European languages.
Mamihlapinatapai (Yaghan, n.): a look shared between two people who both want something but neither will initiate. The Guinness record-holder for most meaning packed into one word.
On October 12, 1810, Bavaria held its first Oktoberfest. The German word 'Gemütlichkeit' — warm conviviality, impossible to fully translate — was born for exactly such occasions.
On this date in 2008, Satoshi Nakamoto sent the Bitcoin whitepaper to the cryptography mailing list. The email's subject line was simply: 'Bitcoin P2P e-cash paper.'
On Oct 12, 2021, the Coinbase NFT waitlist hit 1.5 million signups in 48 hours — before the platform had written a single line of its front-end code.
Bitcoin's UTXO model means your wallet balance doesn't exist. What exists are discrete unspent outputs, like physical coins. Your 'balance' is software arithmetic performed at read time.

The DAO hack of 2016 didn't exploit a bug in Ethereum — it exploited the contract code exactly as written. The code was the bug. Ethereum's immutability principle then had to be argued away to reverse it.
Hal Finney received the first Bitcoin transaction ever sent — 10 BTC from Satoshi on Jan 12, 2009 — while already suffering from ALS, a diagnosis he had not yet made public.

On this date in 1950, Alan Turing's 'Computing Machinery and Intelligence' was published in Mind — the paper that introduced the imitation game and framed machine intelligence as a behavioral, not metaphysical, question.
On this date in 2012, Krizhevsky's AlexNet entry was submitted to ImageNet. Its 10.8-point error gap over second place was so large that organizers initially suspected a reporting mistake.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 GWh of electricity — comparable to the annual residential energy use of about 4,600 American homes.

Transformers were not invented for language. The 2017 'Attention Is All You Need' paper targeted neural machine translation; its authors did not anticipate the architecture would become the substrate for most of modern AI.

DeepMind's AlphaFold 2 predicted structures for over 200 million proteins — essentially the entire known proteome — in a database released freely in 2022, a dataset that took the prior century of crystallography to partially assemble.
